task: Fix Cleanup merged branches workflow failing with HTTP 422 when a proven-merged branch is deleted concurrently by GitHub's delete-branch-on-merge

events.summary: GitHub notification: run 34863519980 (PR #176 merge event) failed in sweep-merged-heads with urllib.error.HTTPError 422 raised from the git/refs DELETE call; the four later runs on the same workflow succeeded.
events.provenance: gh run view 34863519980 --log-failed; gh run list --workflow cleanup-merged-branch.yml

events.summary: Only the HTTPError handler around the DELETE call changes: 422 with body 'Reference does not exist' is treated like 404 (branch already gone) and recorded as retained/already-deleted. Selection logic, permissions, and triggers are untouched.

Before changing anything: the failed run's traceback ends in the DELETE branch (script line 28 -> req line 6) with HTTP 422; at that moment the same three branches were being removed by GitHub's delete-branch-on-merge from `gh pr merge --delete-branch`, and GitHub's git/refs DELETE returns 422 'Reference does not exist' for a missing ref, which the handler only tolerated as 404. The next four merge-event runs, with no concurrent deletion, all succeeded, matching the race explanation.
Handler now reads the error body and treats 404, or 422 whose body contains 'Reference does not exist', as already deleted (logged under retained as already-deleted); every other error still raises.

scripts/ci/check-mutable-inputs.py passed for the workflow; the embedded Python was extracted from the YAML and compiled with compile(); no Go, chart, or Dockerfile changed so the Go/CI suites are unaffected by this diff.
events.scope: Static verification only. The race itself was not re-created live; confirmation is the next merged-PR run of Cleanup merged branches being green.

events.summary: Cleanup merged branches tolerates refs already removed by another actor; gate.py passes for this trace against baseline.eval.json.
Fix committed and statically verified; live confirmation comes from the next merged-PR run of the workflow.
events.next: Watch the Cleanup merged branches run on this PR's own merge event.
